purpose: Podofilox is used to treat genital warts (also called condyloma acuminata) that appear on the outside of the genitals. It helps get rid of the wart tissue by destroying the wart cells. It is applied directly to the warts and is not used for warts inside the vagina, cervix, or rectum.
how_it_works: Podofilox works by stopping wart cells from dividing and multiplying, which causes the wart tissue to die and eventually fall off. Think of it like cutting off the fuel supply the wart cells need to grow. Over time, the treated warts shrink and disappear.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or pain at the application site is very common, especially in the first few days. You may also notice redness, swelling, itching, or soreness where you applied it. Some people experience skin erosion or a raw feeling in the treated area.
warnings: Only apply this medicine to the exact warts your doctor pointed out — do not put it on healthy skin, open sores, or mucous membranes inside the body. Do not use more than directed, as using too much can cause serious side effects. This medication must NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm an unborn baby. Keep it away from your eyes and wash your hands thoroughly after each use.
typical_dosing: Apply a small amount to the warts twice a day (morning and evening) for 3 days in a row, then stop using it for 4 days. This 3-days-on and 4-days-off schedule counts as one treatment cycle. You may repeat up to 4 cycles total. Use only the amount needed to cover the warts — usually no more than 0.5 mL per day.
